newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Trial in Vietnam drug scandal set for next month.
newsitem.headline: Trial in Vietnam drug scandal set for next month.

text.p: The trial of state police officials and dozens of other alleged members of an international heroin trafficking ring will open in Hanoi early next month, an prosecution official said on Saturday.
The official, who declined to be named, said the Hanoi People's Court hearing would open on May 2 or May 4 and last eight to 10 days.

A report in the state-controlled daily Vietnam News said 40 people would stand trial for bringing 141 kg (310 pounds) of heroin and hundreds of kilograms of opium into the country from Thailand via Laos.
The drugs scandal, Vietnam's biggest yet, broke last year when convicted Laotian trafficker Sieng Pheng earned a last-minute reprieve from execution in return for information.
His confessions led to the arrest of about 30 people, including several Interior Ministry police and border guards.
Pheng said that the 15 kg (33 pounds) of heroin found in the seats of a car was just part of his delivery and that more had been concealed in a false bottom of the car's fuel tank.
Five police officers, including Interior Ministry Captain Vu Xuan Truong, were charged with stealing after the fuel tank was found to be empty.
According to official media reports, police found $100,000 in cash, 5.1 kg (11.2 pounds) or heroin and guns at Truong's house.

Vietnam News said that in addition to the 40 who will stand trial, the Police Investigation Department had issued arrest warrants for 34 suspects, including 12 police officers, four border guards and a foreigner.

The government says it is concerned that Vietnam is being targetted by international drug syndicates as a conduit and market for illegal narcotics from the notorious Golden Triangle region which borders Vietnam, Laos and China.
